launcher.home.desc:
Draws the sounds you can't see right on your screen.
From gaming to movies, try a whole new experience.
settings.visual_mode.title: Visual mode
settings.visual_mode.desc: Choose the basic shape of the graphics drawn on screen.
settings.sound_mode.title: Sound mode
settings.sound_mode.desc:
Choose the sound channels that match your speakers.
For 2-channel speakers, choose '2 channels'. For surround speakers, choose '5.1 channels' or '7.1 channels'.
settings.max_fps.title: Max frame rate
settings.max_fps.desc: Sets the highest frame rate the graphics are drawn at.
settings.size_lock.title: Lock size
settings.size_lock.desc: Keeps the graphics at a fixed size and shows loudness through their transparency instead.
settings.fixed_size.desc: Sets the fixed size the graphics stay at while their transparency changes.
settings.max_opacity.title: Max opacity
settings.max_opacity.desc: How opaque the graphics get at the loudest sound.
settings.size.title: Size
settings.size.desc.wave: Adjusts the height of the wave and how full it looks overall.
settings.size.desc.pad: Adjusts how thick and wide the pads get when they react to sound.
settings.size.desc.circle: Adjusts how far the circle equalizer bulges out when sound plays.
settings.size.desc.outline: Adjusts the height of the outline wave and how full it looks overall.
settings.opacity.title: Opacity
settings.opacity.desc.wave: Higher values draw the wave bolder; lower values let more of the game or screen behind it show through.
settings.opacity.desc.pad: Higher values draw the pads bolder; lower values make them fainter and more transparent.
settings.opacity.desc.circle: Higher values draw the circle bolder; lower values make it fainter and more transparent.
settings.opacity.desc.outline: Higher values draw the outline wave bolder; lower values make it fainter and more transparent.
settings.speed.title: Speed
settings.speed.desc.wave: Adjusts how fast the wave flows and ripples.
settings.speed.desc.pad: Adjusts how fast the pads turn toward the direction a sound comes from.
settings.speed.desc.circle: Adjusts how fast the circle equalizer ripples and turns in response to sound.
settings.speed.desc.outline: Adjusts how fast the outline wave flows and ripples.
settings.sensitivity.title: Sensitivity
settings.sensitivity.desc.wave: Adjusts how sensitively the wave reacts and surges, even to quiet sounds.
settings.sensitivity.desc.pad: Adjusts the pads so they pick up sound better and stand out more.
settings.sensitivity.desc.circle: Adjusts how finely the circle's amplitude breaks up as it reacts to sound.
settings.sensitivity.desc.outline: Adjusts how sensitively the outline wave reacts and surges, even to quiet sounds.
settings.glow.title: Glow
settings.glow.desc.wave:
Adds a soft neon glow along the edge of the wave and adjusts its strength.
Note: uses extra GPU resources.
settings.glow.desc.pad:
Adds a soft, aura-like glow around the pads.
Note: uses extra GPU resources.
settings.glow.desc.circle:
Adds a shimmering halo along the edge of the circle equalizer.
Note: uses extra GPU resources.
settings.glow.desc.outline:
Adds a soft neon glow to the outline and adjusts its strength.
Note: uses extra GPU resources.
settings.radius.title: Radius
settings.radius.desc: Sets the radius of the center ring in Circle mode.
settings.hotkey.visual.title: Switch visual mode
settings.hotkey.visual.desc: Hotkey that changes the shape in real time while running.
settings.hotkey.sound.title: Switch sound mode
settings.hotkey.sound.desc: Hotkey that changes the sound mode in real time while running.
settings.hotkey.edit.title: Overlay settings
settings.hotkey.edit.desc: Hotkey that opens or closes the overlay editor.
settings.developer_mode.title: Developer mode
settings.developer_mode.desc: Shows debug information and the audio engine status on screen.
settings.auto_minimize.title: Minimize launcher on start
settings.auto_minimize.desc: Automatically minimizes this launcher window when the overlay starts.
sounds.title: Choose sound types
sounds.desc: Sounds the AI recognizes are grouped with similar sounds, under the type each counts as by default. Change a group’s type, and the color of its sounds follows right away.
sounds.sibling_note: The AI often hears one sound under several names at once. A siren, for example, is also heard as “Alarm”, which is in another group. If a sound still shows its old type after a change, change the related groups or sounds too.
sounds.advanced.title: Advanced mode
sounds.advanced.desc: Shows every sound in its group, so you can change sounds one by one.
sounds.reset.title: Reset all sounds?
sounds.reset.message: Every sound you changed goes back to its default type.
sounds.group.mixed_note: Some sounds changed one by one
sounds.overwrite.title: Change the whole group?
sounds.overwrite.message: Sounds in the “{0}” group that will change to {2}: {1}. Sounds you changed one by one are overwritten too.
sounds.basic_warning.title: Switch to basic mode?
sounds.basic_warning.message: Some groups have sounds you changed one by one. In basic mode, choosing a type for one of these groups gives every sound in it that type, and your one-by-one changes in that group are overwritten. Nothing changes until you choose.
help.start.title: Getting started
help.start.1: Pick your language at the top of this window, and change how the graphics look in the Settings tab if you like.
help.start.3: The graphics are drawn along the edges of the screen, on top of other windows such as games and videos. Clicks pass through them, so you can keep using the window underneath.
help.start.4: To turn it off, click “{0}” on Home, or right-click the Sound Visualizer icon in the notification area of the taskbar and choose “{0}”.
help.modes.title: Visual modes
help.mode.wave: The whole edge of the screen pushes inward with the loudness. The side the sound comes from pushes in deeper.
help.mode.pad: Bars light up at 8 spots around the edge of the screen. Shows direction most clearly.
help.mode.circle: A ring in the center of the screen swells toward the sound.
help.mode.outline: Draws only a thin outline of the wave, so it covers less of your game.
help.modes.note: Settings like size and opacity are saved separately for each mode and can be changed in the Settings tab.
help.sound.title: Sound types
help.sound.kinds: AI sorts what you hear into ambient, speech and danger sounds. By default, ambient is white, speech is yellow and danger is red. You can change the color of each type and whether it's shown in the Settings tab.
help.sound.groups: In the Sounds tab, similar sounds are grouped, and you pick which type each group counts as. For example, change the “Doorbell” group to Danger, and when the AI hears a doorbell or a knock it gets the danger color. A sound you newly set to Danger only takes part in the AI's vote on the type, though, so this doesn't mean every doorbell will be shown as danger.
help.sound.advanced: Turn on Advanced mode to change sounds one by one.
help.sound.danger: When a danger sound (like a gunshot) is detected, the color changes instantly instead of fading.
help.pc.title: PC settings and hotkeys
help.sound_mode.title: Sound mode
help.sound_mode.body: For direction (radar) to work properly, your output device must be set to '5.1 Surround' (6 channels) or '7.1 Surround' (8 channels) in the Windows sound settings. With ordinary stereo (2 channels), the graphics may only appear on the left and right. To make up for this, set 'Sound mode' to match in the Settings tab.
help.sound_mode.tip: 💡 If you don't have a 7.1 output device, you can install the {0} and set the output device to 7.1 channels to show the overlay with 7.1 surround sound.
help.hotkeys.title: Real-time custom hotkeys
help.hotkeys.body: In the Settings tab, click a hotkey button and press a single key or a key combination (e.g. Ctrl + Shift + A) to change the hotkey as you like. Pressing the hotkey, even while the app is in the background, switches the mode instantly.
help.hotkeys.defaults: By default, F2 switches the sound mode, F3 switches the visual mode and F4 opens the overlay settings.
help.size_lock.title: Lock size mode
help.size_lock.body: Lock size mode keeps the graphics at a fixed size by using transparency in proportion to the loudness of the sound. It's useful when you want to keep the graphics the same size while still seeing them react to sound.
help.editor.title: Real-time overlay edit mode
help.editor.body: Press the assigned hotkey (F4 by default) to turn on the overlay edit mode. You can drag on the screen with your mouse to adjust the size limit of the graphics, and fine-tune the details in the settings panel that pops up.
help.developer.title: Developer mode
help.developer.body: Turning on Developer mode adds technical information to the overlay, such as the detailed AI label being detected, the live channel status of the audio engine, and the FPS. It's useful when you want to check that the system is working properly.
help.notes.title: Good to know
help.note.direction_surround: With 5.1 or 7.1 channel output, the top of the screen shows sound from the front and the bottom shows sound from behind. The left and right sides show sound from the left and right, and graphics coming from every side at once are ambient or non-directional sounds.
help.note.direction_stereo: With 2-channel (stereo) output, it can tell left from right, but not front from back, so the graphics appear only on the left and right sides.
help.note.sources: It shows the sound of every app that plays through the default playback device in Windows. Sound that an app sends to another device, such as a headset used only for voice chat, isn't shown.
help.note.volume: If an app's volume is turned down very low or muted, in the app itself or in the Windows volume mixer, its sound may barely show or not show at all. If the graphics don't respond well, turn that sound up a little or raise Sensitivity in the Settings tab.
help.note.ai: AI classification can be wrong. Don't rely on this app as your only safeguard when safety is at stake.
help.faq.title: FAQ
help.faq.stopped_q: It turned off without me stopping it.
help.faq.stopped_a: It turns off when sound capture stops and doesn't recover within a few seconds, for example when the playback device is disconnected and no other device is available. Home then shows why. Connect speakers or headphones, or set a default playback device in the Windows sound settings, then start it again.
help.faq.no_graphic_a: Check that the sound is playing through the default playback device in Windows and isn't muted, and whether Home shows a notice. If a game runs in exclusive full-screen mode, try its borderless or windowed mode. Also make sure opacity isn't too low in Settings, and that showing the current sound type isn't turned off.
help.faq.performance_q: Does it use a lot of CPU or GPU?
help.faq.performance_a: To make it lighter, lower “{0}” in the Settings tab or turn off “{1}”.
help.faq.language_q: How do I change the app language?
help.faq.language_a: Pick one from the “{0}” list at the top of this window. While the visualizer is running, you can also change it in the overlay settings. “{1}” follows the Windows display language.
help.report.title: Report a problem
help.report.desc: Tell us about a bug, or a sound that was shown as the wrong type. GitHub opens in your browser with the environment info below filled in, so it needs a GitHub account. Without one, send us an email instead. No audio is ever sent.
help.report.copy_failed: Couldn't copy to the clipboard. Try again.
help.report.no_browser: Couldn't open a browser. Copy the environment info and send it to us instead.
help.report.no_mail: No email app to send with. Copy the environment info and send it another way.
help.report.issue_body:
What happened?

What were you listening to (app, kind of sound)?

What did you expect instead?

help.licenses.title: Open source licenses
notice.ai_unavailable: Sound type detection isn't working, so every sound is shown in the ambient color. Try turning the visualizer off and on again.
notice.ai_unavailable_hidden: Sound type detection isn't working, so every sound counts as ambient, and ambient sounds are turned off, so nothing is shown. Turn on “{0}” in the Settings tab, or try turning the visualizer off and on again.
notice.stopped.title: Sound visualizer turned off
notice.stopped.no_device: No playback device could be opened, so sound can't be captured. Connect speakers or headphones, or set a default playback device in the Windows sound settings, then start again.
notice.stopped.capture_error: Sound capture stopped because of an error, so the graphics are off.
more_info.title: GitHub repository and contributing
more_info.body: Sound Visualizer is an open-source project, and its source code is public on GitHub. You can take part by reporting bugs, suggesting features, or contributing to development. Click the button below to visit the official GitHub repository! You can also check for and download the latest version on the Releases tab on GitHub.
